comment: Source of truth for Jinja2C++'s third-party inventory (docs/tasks/0187). Edit this file, then run scripts/sbom.py to regenerate the CycloneDX and SPDX documents next to it; scripts/sbom.py --check (format-check CI) fails when they are stale, when a pin below no longer matches the build files, or when the build gains a dependency this file does not list. Vocabulary and the reasoning per component: docs/dependencies.md.

components.name: expected-lite
components.used_for: nonstd::expected behind jinja2::Result<T> in every Load/Render signature (include/jinja2cpp/template.h, template_env.h); make_unexpected in parsers and bindings
components.why: C++17 has no std::expected; the 2.0 API returns Result<T> (docs/api-2.0.md decision 4), and Clang 18 + libstdc++ at C++23 ships <expected> without std::expected
components.lighten: Keep until a C++23 floor. Header-only and small; could be vendored into include/ so consumers need nothing extra, at the cost of an ODR clash with a consumer's own expected-lite of another version

components.name: fmt
components.used_for: Python str.format / format filter and %-formatting (src/python_format.cpp, serialize_filters.cpp, value_methods.cpp), number-to-string, wide-string formatting (fmt/xchar.h), error messages (error_info.cpp), the string builder's memory_buffer
components.why: Python's format-spec mini-language with runtime format strings, precision-as-argument and wchar_t output; std::format is C++20 and the floor is C++17
components.lighten: Keep. Could be built header-only (FMT_HEADER_ONLY) to remove the link-time dependency of static consumers, at a compile-time cost; replace with std::format only at a C++20 floor (wide output and runtime specs still need checking)

components.name: boost
components.selected_by: always (internal mode builds it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75)
components.used_for: See the boost-* sub-components: 9 libraries are used directly; internal mode pulls 47 and installs all of them (56 MB of headers, 4 static libraries)
components.why: Historically the portability layer for pre-C++17 (any, optional, variant, filesystem, string algorithms); today mostly small utilities that C++17 lacks (span, small_vector, intrusive_ptr, move-only any) plus Boost.JSON as the default metadata parser
components.lighten: The largest weight by far and the main target. Every directly used piece has a small replacement (see sub-components); a Boost-free core is feasible without behaviour change (docs/tasks/0230)

components.name: boost-core
components.used_for: boost::span over node arrays, arguments and slots (about 57 uses in 14 src/ files: node_arena.h, statements.cpp, render_context.h)
components.lighten: Replace with a 50-line internal span (or std::span behind a C++20 switch)

components.name: boost-container
components.used_for: small_vector in parsers, evaluator, name resolver and render context (about 27 uses in 10 src/ files); header-only use, but the internal modes build and link boost_container.a (named explicitly since lexical_cast stopped pulling it in)
components.why: Inline-storage vector that avoids heap allocations on hot paths (perf track 0117/0118)
components.lighten: Header-only use; replaceable by an internal small_vector, but it is perf-sensitive, so measure with bench/ (Cachegrind gate) before swapping

components.name: boost-smart_ptr
components.used_for: intrusive_ptr for InternalValue's shared payloads and the render workspace (internal_value.h, render_workspace.h; about 26 uses)
components.why: One pointer wide with the count inside the object, which the 32-byte InternalValue layout (0140) relies on; std::shared_ptr is two pointers
components.lighten: Replace with an internal intrusive_ptr (about 60 lines)

components.name: boost-any
components.used_for: boost::anys::unique_any holds the parsed JSON metadata document of whichever JSON backend is compiled in (template_impl.h:801, binding/*_parser.h); boost::any_cast in rapid_json_parser.h
components.why: Move-only type erasure; std::any requires copyable payloads
components.lighten: Replace with std::unique_ptr to a small polymorphic holder, or drop when metadata parsing gets one fixed parser

components.name: boost-iterator
components.used_for: iterator_facade for one internal iterator (internal_value.h:1250)
components.why: Less boilerplate for a conforming iterator
components.lighten: Write the iterator by hand (about 40 lines)

components.name: boost-filesystem
components.used_for: path joining and last_write_time in RealFileSystem (src/filesystem_handler.cpp:131-170); compiled library plus boost_atomic
components.why: Pre-C++17 history; nothing Boost-specific is used
components.lighten: Replace with std::filesystem (C++17): removes two compiled libraries; check the file_time_type to time_t conversion and old toolchains needing -lstdc++fs

components.name: boost-algorithm
components.used_for: replace_all/replace_first and is_alnum in string_converter_filter.cpp, all()+is_space in template_parser.h
components.lighten: Replace with a few lines of std::string code

components.name: boost-predef
components.used_for: BOOST_ENDIAN_BIG_BYTE to pick RapidJSON's UTF-16/32 encoding (rapid_json_parser.h:29), included from template_impl.h
components.why: Byte order detection before C++20 std::endian
components.lighten: Replace with a compiler-macro check (__BYTE_ORDER__ / _WIN32)

components.name: boost-json
components.used_for: Parses {% meta %} JSON metadata for Template::GetMetadata (template_impl.h:484-498, binding/boost_json_parser.h); the opt-in adapter header include/jinja2cpp/binding/boost_json.h converts boost::json::value to jinja2::Value
components.why: One of three interchangeable JSON backends; the default because Boost is already required
components.lighten: The heaviest backend (boost_json.a + boost_container.a, about 4.8 MB in a Debug build) for a niche feature (template metadata). An internal minimal JSON reader, or nlohmann as default, would remove both libraries; the adapter headers stay opt-in

components.name: boost-multiprecision
components.selected_by: JINJA2CPP_WITH_BIGINT=boost (default none) compiles it into src/big_int_builtin.cpp; the tests always build the adapter. Standalone mode (BOOST_MP_STANDALONE): only Multiprecision and Config headers, taken from the Boost release of the deps mode
components.used_for: cpp_int behind the built-in big-integer backend (exact integer arithmetic beyond int64, docs/tasks/0272); the opt-in header-only adapter include/jinja2cpp/big_int/boost_cpp_int.h is also the sample backend
components.why: A mature header-only arbitrary-precision integer; the library calls a backend only through the BigIntBackend table (include/jinja2cpp/big_int_backend.h), so any library can replace it at run time
components.lighten: Header-only, no link cost, off by default. After 0230 drops Boost from the core, fetch boostorg/multiprecision and boostorg/config on their own (docs/design/0178-big-integer-plan.md section 8)

components.name: nlohmann_json
components.selected_by: JINJA2CPP_WITH_JSON_BINDINGS=nlohmann; also fetched whenever JINJA2CPP_BUILD_TESTS is ON (tests, parity corpus and bench read JSON with it)
components.used_for: Metadata parser when selected (binding/nlohmann_json_parser.h); opt-in adapter include/jinja2cpp/binding/nlohmann_json.h; test data (tojson, metadata, parity corpus) and bench case files
components.why: Header-only JSON backend alternative; the test suite's JSON reader
components.lighten: Header-only, no link cost. The cheapest default backend if Boost.JSON goes

components.name: RapidJSON
components.used_for: Metadata parser when selected (binding/rapid_json_parser.h); opt-in adapter include/jinja2cpp/binding/rapid_json.h
components.why: Third JSON backend alternative for users who already carry RapidJSON
components.lighten: Header-only. Patched locally, and the conan-build mode takes an unpatched ConanCenter snapshot; upstream has had no release since 2016. A candidate to retire as a built-in backend while keeping the adapter header

components.name: robin-hood-hashing
components.modified: try_emplace_transparent added (0118 P5b-3b); allocation through ::operator new/delete (0154); exception safety of inserts, growth and copies (0253); documented at src/robin_hood.h:41-51
components.used_for: InternalValueMap and scope tables (internal_value.h:1345, render_context.h), robin_hood::hash_bytes
components.why: Flat open-addressing map, measurably faster than std::unordered_map on the render paths
components.lighten: Upstream is archived and recommends its successor ankerl::unordered_dense (MIT); boost::unordered_flat_map is the other candidate while Boost stays. Not a size issue, a maintenance one (docs/tasks/0231)

components.name: lexertk
components.modified: Modified by Flex Ferrum (2018), changes not recorded (src/lexertk.h:6); upstream version not recorded
components.used_for: Expression tokenizer behind src/lexer.h, renderer.h and template_parser.h
components.why: Ready-made C-like tokenizer the expression parser was built on
components.lighten: Small and internal; keep. Long term it is effectively forked code and could be absorbed as project code with its notice kept

components.name: value_types
components.modified: both at upstream 57f2e7a, moved to namespace jinja2::v2::detail::xyz with JINJA2CPP_XYZ_ macros (0076); indirect: Clang incomplete-type fix (0edc34d), tag tested first (0072); polymorphic: default constructor constrained on the allocator for MSVC std::variant (0071), cb_ initialised (0089), in-place initializer_list constructor creates U, not T
components.used_for: polymorphic and indirect (jinja2::v2::detail::xyz) behind jinja2::types and jinja2::detail (value_ptr.h), used by Value, GenericList and GenericMap
components.why: Value-semantic owning pointers for the public value model; standardised as std::indirect/std::polymorphic in C++26
components.lighten: Keep (header-only, installed). Switch to std:: at a C++26 floor

components.name: Unicode Character Database (via Python unicodedata)
components.used_for: Code-point tables for str.isprintable/isalpha/..., upper/lower/title/casefold, int() digit handling
components.why: Python-identical string predicates and case mapping without ICU
components.lighten: Data only, no dependency at build time (Python is needed only to regenerate). Acquisition decision is still open in docs/tasks/0187 and 0186

components.name: HTML5 named character references (via Python html.entities)
components.supplier: Python Software Foundation (table from the WHATWG HTML standard)
components.used_for: Entity table for MarkupSafe-compatible unescape/striptags
components.why: Same entity set as Python's html.unescape
components.lighten: Data only; keep

components.name: googletest
components.selected_by: JINJA2CPP_BUILD_TESTS (ON for the main project); a system GTest is preferred
components.used_for: The jinja2cpp_tests binary
components.lighten: Test-only. Fetched by a mutable git tag, not a hash
